items.prompt_en: Read these lines aloud with a clap on the beat: 'Papa looks under the sofa, / Papa looks behind the door.' Where do you take a small pause?

items.answer: At the end of the first line, after 'sofa'
acceptable: at the end of each line
hints: Say the first line. Where does your voice want to rest?
Look for the little comma mark.
Pa-pa looks un-der the so-fa — and pause?
We pause after 'sofa', at the end of the line.

items.prompt_en: Listen: 'He peeps inside the sugar tin / And crawls along the floor. / "Where are my specs?" he grumbles.' What is Papa looking for?
items.prompt_hi: Suno — Papa sugar tin mein aur floor par kya dhoondh rahe hain?
items.answer: His specs (spectacles)
hints: What does Papa ask in the last line?
He asks 'Where are my ___?'
It is something you wear on your eyes: sp___.

items.prompt_en: Listen: 'head' and 'said'. The letters at the end are different. Do they rhyme?

items.answer: Yes
hints: Say both words slowly.
Listen only to the ending sound.
h-ead, s-aid: is the end sound the same?
Yes. Head and said end with the same sound, so they rhyme.

items.prompt_en: Listen: "'I've searched the house all day!' / ... They never went away!" Which word rhymes with 'day'?

items.answer: away
hints: Listen to the last word of each line.
One line ends with 'day'. How does the other line end?
It ends with 'went a___'.
'Day' rhymes with 'away'.

items.prompt_en: Listen: "'Where are my specs?' he grumbles, / 'I've searched the house all day!'" Mummy is trying not to laugh. What do you think Mummy can see that Papa cannot?

items.answer: The specs are on Papa's head

Papa is wearing them on his head
hints: Why would Mummy want to laugh?
Mummy can see Papa's whole face and head.

items.prompt_en: The specs were on Papa's head all along. Why is that funny?

they were with him the whole time
we can see them but Papa can't

Where were the specs while he searched?
Could Papa see his own head? Could we?

items.prompt_en: Fill in 'is' or 'are': Papa's spectacles ___ on his head.

Papa's spectacles are on his head.

items.prompt_en: Make your own sentence about scissors, like 'Papa's spectacles are on his head.' Where are the scissors in your house?

items.answer: A sentence using 'scissors are', for example 'The scissors are in the drawer.'
acceptable: The scissors are on the table.

items.answer: Spectacles and glasses

One word is long and starts with 'spec'.

items.prompt_en: Which line should you say in a bigger, surprised voice: 'Papa looks behind the door' or 'But high upon his head they sit'? Why?

items.answer: 'But high upon his head they sit', because it is the surprise ending

items.prompt_en: Your little cousin did not get the joke in the poem. Explain to her in two or three sentences what happens and why it is funny.
items.prompt_hi: Tumhari chhoti cousin ko joke samajh nahi aaya. Use do-teen sentences mein samjhao — kya hua aur funny kyun hai.
items.answer: Papa looks for his specs all over the house; they were on his head the whole time; it is funny because everyone could see them except Papa
acceptable: Papa searched everywhere but the specs were on his head
he couldn't find what he was already wearing

Where does he look?

items.prompt_en: Listen: 'One Sunday, Dadaji parked his old blue scooter near the village fair and went to buy jalebis.' Where did Dadaji park the scooter?

acceptable: the scooter goes off with Chintu

Is anyone holding the handle who knows how to ride?
The story's title says the scooter is 'gone'...

items.answer: The scooter rolled down the slope.
hints: Did this happen now or before?

Add the past ending: roll + __.
The scooter rolled down the slope.

items.prompt_en: Which is right: 'Dadaji goed to the shop' or 'Dadaji went to the shop'?
items.prompt_hi: Kaunsa sahi — 'goed' ya 'went'?
items.answer: Dadaji went to the shop
